papers.title: DARI BUKU MENUJU PENGALAMAN BELAJAR MENDALAM: ANALISIS KUALITAS BUKU MATEMATIKA KELAS V BERPERSPEKTIF ACTIVE DEEP LEARNER EXPERIENCE (ADLX)
papers.abstract: Pendekatan Active Deep Learner eXperience (ADLX) telah diterapkan dalam pembelajaran, namun kajian terhadap kualitas buku ajar sebagai pendukung implementasinya masih terbatas. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis kualitas Buku Matematika Kelas V JSIT Indonesia pada materi bilangan dalam mendukung ADLX. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan deskriptif kualitatif dengan metode analisis isi (content analysis). Buku dianalisis berdasarkan aspek kelayakan isi, penyajian, bahasa, dan kegrafikan yang selanjutnya diinterpretasikan melalui komponen Active Learning, Deep Learning, dan Learner eXperience. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa buku memiliki kualitas yang baik dalam mendukung ketiga komponen ADLX. Kelayakan isi mendukung Deep Learning melalui kesesuaian materi dengan capaian pembelajaran, pengembangan konsep secara bertahap, dan penerapan konsep dalam konteks kehidupan nyata. Kelayakan penyajian memfasilitasi Active Learning melalui eksplorasi, diskusi, presentasi, dan pemecahan masalah, sedangkan penggunaan bahasa yang komunikatif mendukung keterlibatan dan pemahaman konsep. Kegrafikan melalui ilustrasi, tata letak, dan keterbacaan turut mendukung Learner eXperience. Namun, aktivitas pembelajaran masih cenderung terstruktur, soal terbuka dan investigasi mandiri masih terbatas, serta konteks lokal belum dimanfaatkan secara optimal. Dengan demikian, buku berpotensi mendukung implementasi ADLX, tetapi masih memerlukan penguatan aktivitas eksploratif, investigatif, dan pemanfaatan konteks lokal.

papers.title: Implant-Abutment Connection Design and Patient-Centered Outcomes: Bridging Biomechanical and Biological Performance with Patient Experience - A Critical Narrative Review
papers.abstract: Dental implant therapy has evolved from a survival-centered treatment philosophy toward a broader concept of success that incorporates biological stability, prosthetic reliability, function, esthetics, and patient satisfaction (1,2). The implant-abutment connection (IAC) is a critical component of the implant-prosthetic complex because connection geometry can influence load transfer, micromotion, screw-joint stability, microgap formation, microbial leakage, peri-implant tissue behavior, marginal bone remodeling, and technical complications (3-9). Systematic reviews and meta-analyses generally demonstrate more favorable marginal bone preservation with internal and particularly conical connection configurations than with traditional external hexagonal systems, whereas differences in implant survival are less consistent and survival remains high across modern systems (7,8,10). Despite extensive evidence on biomechanical and clinician-reported outcomes, comparatively little research directly evaluates whether connection-specific advantages are perceptible to patients (33,37-43). Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs), including comfort, masticatory function, esthetic satisfaction, overall satisfaction, and oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL), therefore provide an essential complementary perspective (33,35,37-43). This critical narrative review integrates mechanistic, biological, clinical, and patient-reported evidence and proposes a three-level framework distinguishing direct PROM evidence from clinically mediated and mechanistic outcomes. Current evidence supports favorable joint stability, sealing behavior, and marginal bone outcomes for well-designed internal conical connections, but conical and Morse-taper systems are heterogeneous and differ in taper angle, indexing, engagement geometry, machining tolerance, and screw design (11). Importantly, randomized abutment-management studies demonstrate that measurable improvements in marginal bone behavior may occur without significant differences in PROMs (25,26). Thus, biomechanical or radiographic superiority should not automatically be interpreted as patient-perceived superiority. Future trials should directly compare connection geometries while simultaneously assessing standardized clinical outcomes and validated PROMs.

papers.title: Belief-based Risk-Aware Anticipatory Navigation: Modeling Intention and Position Uncertainty for Safe and Efficient Robot Navigation
papers.abstract: The increasing deployment of Automated Mobile Vehicles (AMVs) in warehouses requires efficient navigation in dynamic environments shared with human workers. Traditional safety strategies, such as stopping or slowing down, often reduce efficiency and do not account for human-robot interaction. To address this, interaction-aware methods have been developed. However, traditional interaction models assume fixed parameters, rely on a single forecast, or use intent labels that are not updated during the interaction, and thus do not explicitly represent intention uncertainty, that is, variability in how people react to robots. When combined with position uncertainty introduced by sensing noise, this unmodeled intention uncertainty can make motion prediction and navigation decisions unreliable, leading to conservative behavior, inefficiency, or collisions in human–robot interactions. To bridge this gap, we propose Belief-based Risk-Aware Anticipatory Navigation (BRAN), a framework that jointly models intention and position uncertainty. BRAN maintains probabilistic beliefs over an agent's position and intention to explicitly represent uncertainty in both quantities. Position uncertainty is represented via sampled observations, and the intent belief is updated online through Bayesian inference so that predictions evolve with the interaction. These beliefs are propagated through the Social Force Model (SFM) to generate predictions of possible agent motion under uncertainty. We then compute collision risk from the predicted motion distribution and incorporate it into model predictive control as a constraint. This constrains predicted collision risk while optimizing motion toward the goal. Experimental results validate the proposed design in controlled settings, demonstrate its effectiveness in scenarios with multiple pedestrians, and confirm its feasibility on a real robot with onboard sensing and actuation.

papers.title: AgroGuard AI: A Trustworthy Adaptive Architecture for Crop Disease Intelligence under Environmental Non-Stationarity
papers.abstract: Deep learning systems for crop disease recognition are routinely reported at above 95% accuracy on curated benchmarks, yet their field performance degrades sharply and silently once deployed. The cause is not a modelling deficiency in the conventional sense but a violation of the stationarity assumption on which supervised learning rests: the agro-climatic environment that generates the data is itself non-stationary. Humidity regimes shift between seasons, pathogen populations evolve, cultivar mixes change, sensor hardware ages, and the relationship between visual symptom and disease label drifts with them. A model frozen at training time therefore decays monotonically, and — more damagingly for trust — it decays while continuing to report high confidence. This manuscript presents AgroGuard AI, a five-layer reference architecture that treats environmental non-stationarity as a first-class design constraint rather than a deployment nuisance. The architecture couples four mechanisms that are usually studied in isolation. A drift detection subsystem monitors input, representation, and label-conditional distributions using a complementary ensemble of ADWIN, KSWIN, and kernel maximum mean discrepancy tests. A continual learning subsystem combines elastic weight consolidation with sparse episodic replay so that adaptation to a new agro-climatic regime does not erase competence in previously encountered ones. A conformal prediction layer converts raw softmax scores into prediction sets with distribution-free marginal coverage guarantees, and gates low-reliability inputs to human review rather than issuing a confident wrong answer. Finally, a temporal explanation engine reports not only why a prediction was made but why it changed, surfacing the shift in feature attribution that accompanies each adaptation event. We formalise the learning problem, specify each subsystem, derive the adaptation trigger policy, and define a trust metric suite covering calibration error, explanation fidelity, backward transfer, and selective risk. We further specify an edge deployment profile for low-connectivity rural contexts and a privacy-preserving federated aggregation scheme. The manuscript closes with a complete evaluation protocol — datasets, baselines, ablations, and acceptance thresholds — designed to falsify the architecture's central claims. All quantitative values reported herein are design targets and illustrative simulations under explicitly stated generative assumptions; no field trial has been conducted, and this limitation is treated as a defining boundary of the present contribution rather than a caveat.

papers.title: Constraining lunar lower-mantle attenuation using ScSH-SH amplitude ratios
papers.abstract: This repository provides the Python reproduction code accompanying the paper "Constraining lunar lower-mantle attenuation using ScSH-SH amplitude ratios" by Yang and Zhang (Geophysical Journal International, 2026). The code implements a framework for estimating lunar lower-mantle shear-wave quality factor (Q) using the amplitude ratio between ScSH and SH phases recorded at the same seismic station. It includes scripts for spectral analysis, SH-wave radiation pattern computation, geometric spreading and transmission coefficient calculation, narrow-band filtering, Q-value grid-search inversion, and uncertainty quantification via Monte Carlo sampling. The repository also contains text-format data files (travel-time tables, station positions, takeoff angles, and a lunar velocity model) and pre-generated reference figures. Requirements: Python >= 3.9, numpy, matplotlib, scipy, obspy. License: MIT.

papers.title: Fractional two-temperature dual-phase-lag bioheat transfer under electromagnetic heating: An analytical-physics-informed neural network framework
papers.abstract: This study develops a hybrid semi-analytical and physics-informed neural-network framework for transient thermoelastic heat transfer in biological tissue subjected to electromagnetic heating. The formulation combines a fractional two-temperature dual-phase-lag bioheat model with thermoelastic coupling, blood perfusion, temperature-dependent metabolic heat generation, and an effective Maxwell–Ohm Joule-heating source. The governing equations are solved in the Laplace domain and numerically inverted to generate reference temperature, displacement, and stress fields, which are subsequently used to constrain and evaluate a physics-informed neural network. In response to recent experimental evidence on non-Fourier heat transfer in skin, the heat-flux and temperature-gradient phase lags are restricted to an experimentally informed sub-second domain, with baseline values 𝜏 𝑞 = 0 . 2 5 s and 𝜏 𝑇 = 0 . 1 0 s . The results show that fractional thermal memory, conductive–thermodynamic temperature non-equilibrium, and finite-rate transport modify thermal penetration and the timing and magnitude of the thermoelastic response, with the strongest effects concentrated in the rapidly heated near-surface region. The corrected PINN reproduces the semi-analytical thermal and mechanical fields with close field-level agreement within the validated parameter domain, enabling rapid repeated evaluation without replacing the underlying physics-based reference model. Arrhenius post-processing links the corrected transient temperature histories to exposure-time- and depth-dependent thermal-damage measures. The framework therefore provides a computationally efficient tool for sensitivity analysis and model-based thermal-safety assessment. The fractional order and phase-lag parameters are treated as effective, tissue- and protocol-dependent quantities; direct experimental calibration and validation of the complete fractional TTDPL–electromagnetic–thermoelastic model remain necessary before clinical interpretation.

papers.title: Uncertainty-aware prediction of asphalt pavement roughness using probabilistic machine learning
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of asphalt pavement deterioration is critical for data-driven infrastructure asset management. However, conventional data-driven models commonly provide deterministic estimates, offering limited insight into prediction confidence. This limitation restricts their application in risk-aware decision-making, where understanding the reliability of each prediction is essential. This study addresses this challenge by developing an uncertainty-aware framework for predicting pavement roughness using data from the Long-Term Pavement Performance program. A curated dataset of 1,246 test sections across 50 states in the United States was compiled, covering diverse climate regions, structural configurations, traffic loading, and surface characteristics. Probabilistic modeling approaches, including Bayesian neural networks and Gaussian process regression, were used to predict pavement roughness while generating prediction intervals. Deterministic approaches, including random forest, extreme gradient boosting, support vector regression, and artificial neural networks, were also developed under the same validation and optimization framework for benchmarking. All models were evaluated using five-fold cross-validation and optimized using a Bayesian optimization framework. The results showed that extreme gradient boosting achieved the highest point prediction accuracy, while Gaussian process regression and Bayesian neural networks provided competitive accuracy, with coefficients of determination of 0.9133 and 0.9226, respectively, along with explicit uncertainty estimates. Gaussian process regression also demonstrated a reliable uncertainty calibration, with empirical coverage of 95% prediction intervals ranging from 88.89% to 96.31% across climate regions. Initial roughness, rutting, and cracking were identified as the dominant predictors. Regional analyses further revealed generally lower prediction errors in non-freezing regions, and spatial analyses identified geographic variations in pavement deterioration.

papers.title: Energy-efficient dynamic temperature control for frozen plant-based food transport using model predictive control
papers.abstract: Abstract Refrigerated road transport is energy intensive because conventional controllers regulate compartment air temperature reactively while the cargo itself changes temperature slowly. In this work, the potential energy savings from shifting the control reference from air to cargo core temperature are studied using a simulation model of a semi-trailer carrying frozen plant-based food. The controller uses a two-node thermal model to track both the fast air dynamics and the slow cargo thermal response, and a compressor efficiency map to time cooling decisions for periods of higher coefficient of performance. A shrinking prediction horizon matches the remaining transport time, and a two-layer penalty mechanism enforces the frozen-product temperature boundary. Simulation experiments over a 10 h route with door-opening disturbances and ambient temperature variation show that MPC reduces energy consumption from 28.6 to 22.6 kWh, a 21.1% saving, while maintaining the simulated cargo temperature below -18 °C. The saving arises from three control phases: pre-cooling before scheduled door openings, coasting during high-temperature low-efficiency periods, and recovering when ambient conditions improve.

papers.title: The Piece of Wood in Front of Me
papers.abstract: The Piece of Wood in Front of Me: From Average Material Properties to Specimen-Specific Probabilistic Prediction in Wood PhysicsThis essay proposes a specimen-specific perspective on predictive wood physics, organized around a simple question: Can we predict how this particular piece of wood in front of us will behave?Wood science has developed increasingly sophisticated models of heat and moisture transport, anisotropic deformation, drying stresses, hygro-mechanical behavior, and multiphase transport. However, the predictive application of such models to an individual wood specimen remains limited by spatial heterogeneity, incomplete measurements, uncertain constitutive parameters, model-form uncertainty, and the practical impossibility of fully characterizing all internal state variables.The essay argues that future progress should move beyond deterministic forward simulation based on nominal or literature-derived material properties toward specimen-specific, uncertainty-aware prediction. A proposed framework integrates structural characterization, physics-based modeling, sensitivity and identifiability analysis, targeted measurement, inverse inference, Bayesian updating, ensemble prediction, and sequential data assimilation.Recent developments in X-ray CT, 4D CT, hyperspectral imaging, digital image correlation, multiphase transport modeling, hygro-mechanics, and digital-twin concepts are reviewed as emerging components of this framework.The central proposition is that predictive wood science need not know every internal property exactly. Instead, it should determine what must be known for the prediction of interest, what can be inferred from limited observations, what uncertainty remains, and how that uncertainty affects predictive credibility.This document is intended both as a conceptual essay and as a structured reference note for future work on wood heat–moisture transport, deformation, inverse problems, uncertainty quantification, and specimen-specific predictive modeling.

papers.title: Functionally Graded Polymer Lattice Structures Enabled by Multi-Material Fused Deposition Modeling: Current Progress, Challenges, and Future Perspectives
papers.abstract: Functionally graded lattice (FGL) structures can decouple stiffness, strength and energy absorption. Multi-material fused deposition modeling (MM-FDM) is an accessible route to lattices that vary in composition and topology within one print. This review examines MM-FDM polymer FGLs through a PRISMA 2020-informed screening of 610 records. Of the 126 screened references, 65 primary studies meet all eligibility criteria and form the core evidence, and 20 are supporting studies. Four grading strategies were identified: material-based zoning, geometry-induced grading, combined material–geometry grading and process-induced grading, applied mainly to strut-based, triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) and hybrid plate–TPMS architectures. Pairing rigid thermoplastics (PLA, ABS, PETG) with hyperelastic TPU increased specific energy absorption by up to two- to threefold over single-material lattices, but the gain over the rigid constituent alone was smaller and, in several quasi-static studies, negative; it depends on configuration, baseline and loading rate. Graded lattices collapse layer by layer, yet their energy gain over uniform lattices of equal mass is often modest. TPMS architectures are reported to reduce nodal stress concentrations. Most evidence remains at the specimen level. The main limitations are weak interfaces between incompatible polymers, process-induced defects, models that neglect manufacturing effects and the lack of standardized test protocols.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Neural Network-Based Detection of False Data Injection Attacks on FACTS-Assisted Wide-Area Fractional-Order Damping Controllers
papers.abstract: False data injection attacks (FDIAs) pose a serious threat to FACTS-assisted wide-area damping controllers because they corrupt remote measurements, degrade inter-area oscillation damping, and may evade conventional detection. Data-driven detectors that ignore closed-loop physics are particularly vulnerable under multiplicative gain-ramp attacks; the problem is further exacerbated by the memory-dependent nature of fractional-order controllers, whose long-term history effects can mask attack-induced inconsistencies in the residuals unless system dynamics, actuator behavior, attack-channel constraints, and fractional-order memory are jointly embedded in the learning objective. This paper addresses that gap through a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework that jointly estimates latent system states and reconstructs the multiplicative attack gain by incorporating plant dynamics, SVC actuator dynamics, measurement consistency, attack-channel reconstruction, and the reconstructed fractional-order command inside the SVC actuator residual. Detection is declared when a smoothed composite residual exceeds a calibrated threshold. In addition, a supervisory switching mechanism is introduced to replace corrupted wide-area control signals with reconstructed secure equivalents after confirmed detection, thereby restoring closed-loop damping performance without interrupting controller operation. Simulation results on a FACTS-based damping control system under gain-based FDIA scenarios show that the proposed detector achieves up to 99.42% accuracy, 98.86% precision, 99.18% recall, and a 99.02% F1-score, with a false alarm rate as low as 0.53%. The recovery mechanism also substantially reduces post-attack speed-deviation overshoot relative to the unmitigated case.

papers.title: Sources and Strategies for Developing Islamic Cultural History Instructional Materials in Madrasahs: A Systematic Literature Review
papers.abstract: Background: Advances in information technology have driven digital transformation across education, including the subject of Islamic Cultural History (Sejarah Kebudayaan Islam / SKI) in madrasahs, which requires innovative teaching materials to remain relevant to modern learners. Objective: This article aims to analyze various sources and strategies for developing diverse, contextual, and technology-based SKI instructional materials. Method: This study employs a literature review method by collecting, coding, and synthesizing secondary data from ten published scientific journal articles. Results: Effective development of SKI instructional materials relies on integrating national curricula, implementing active learning models (such as project-based learning), utilizing digital media and gamification (e.g., Educaplay and e-learning modules), accommodating student characteristics, and applying research and development (R&D) methodologies (such as the 4D or Borg & Gall models). Conclusion: Technology-based instructional innovations and contextual approaches significantly enhance student engagement, motivation, and comprehension of Islamic historical values. This article provides theoretical and practical contributions as a reference framework for Islamic Education (PAI) teachers and madrasah curriculum developers in designing adaptive, interactive, and effective SKI materials in the digital era. Originality/Value: This review article offers comprehensive novelty in the field of Islamic education and madrasah curriculum development by synthesizing the evolving literature on sources and strategies for designing contextual, technology-based Islamic Cultural History (SKI) instructional materials, an area previously underexplored through a systematic lens. This study maps existing theoretical and methodological gaps while serving as a strategic reference that contributes to developing an adaptive instructional framework and guiding future research agendas on digital media integration in Islamic history education.

papers.title: Multi-Layer Formation Maneuvering Pursuit–Evasion Control for Underactuated Unmanned Surface Vehicles with Uncertainties and Collision Constraints
papers.abstract: Pursuit–evasion tasks involving multiple unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) in complex maritime environments present significant challenges in terms of adaptability, intelligence, and robustness. This paper proposes a novel multi-layer formation control method to significantly improve the maneuverability of USV formation in dynamic pursuit scenarios. The primary contributions of this work are threefold: (1) The development of a maneuverable pursuit–evasion decision layer that enables strategic encirclement of the evader is proposed, which can flexibly adjust the encirclement strategy for the evader and reduce the resource consumption of USVs based on the Apollonius circle-based multiple-angle encirclement strategy and the artificial potential field (APF). (2) A coordination layer based on the trajectory prediction of the evader is designed. This layer introduces a Head-Guidance (HG) operator into the APF to dynamically predict the evader trajectory with motion constraints and assist the Pursuit team to complete tasks. (3) A novel pursuit–evasion distributed Model Predictive Control (MPC) layer that ensures robust formation tracking and collision avoidance is proposed. This layer is specifically engineered to handle not only dynamic obstacle constraints but also lumped uncertainties. The overall performance of the proposed multi-layer framework is verified via abundant numerical simulations under complex marine disturbances and multiple obstacle environments, and the developed fixed-time extended state observer is validated with a real-water field experiment with a single self-developed USV prototype.

papers.title: Learning Memory Operators with Physics-Informed Neural Networks: State Recovery, Kernel Reconstruction, and Parameter Identifiability
papers.abstract: Memory-dependent evolution equations replace the time derivative of the state by a convolution with a memory kernel K(t). They are used in anomalous diffusion, viscoelasticity and tumour-growth modelling, usually with K fixed in advance, most often as the power-law kernel of a Caputo derivative. We study the joint recovery of K and the state u with a physics-informed neural network (PINN) trained by a block-coordinate Variable Projection (VarPro) scheme, for four kernel parametrizations: a non-negative Prony series, a fractional (Caputo) power law, a stretched exponential and a shape-constrained spline. In the best-performing runs on a synthetic benchmark, the state is recovered with relative errors below 0.05% for all four families, while kernel recovery depends strongly on the family. The fractional kernel is recovered almost exactly, the stretched exponential to 5.7%, and the Prony series with a kernel-function reconstruction error of 2–4% in its best runs. A local sensitivity analysis at the exact solution, which requires no training, shows that the individual Prony parameters are severely ill conditioned: the column-normalized condition number of the sensitivity matrix is more than two orders of magnitude larger when the true decay rates are a factor of four apart than when they are well separated. Fitted against the exact state, without a network, the kernel and the three active Prony modes are recovered to a rounding error, while the redundant zero-weight modes of the over-parametrized representation remain non-identifiable. A perturbation of only 0.1% raises the active-mode parameter error to tens of percent while the kernel error stays near 0.1%, and this error tracks the condition number. A Gauss–Newton/Laplace approximation and an eight-replicate training ensemble agree that the rates are far less well determined than K(t). A spline that assumes only positivity, monotonicity and convexity reaches a kernel error of about 6%. The results show that an accurate state does not guarantee accurate recovery of the kernel or of its parameters, and that state accuracy, kernel-function accuracy and parameter identifiability should be assessed separately.

papers.title: Real-time decentralized multi-actuator chassis control strategy for vehicle lateral stability based on nonlinear MPC
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel Decentralized Multi-Actuator Chassis Control (DMCC) strategy for vehicle lateral stability, utilizing real-time Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC). The proposed hierarchical framework decomposes integrated chassis control into a vehicle-level lateral dynamics control and multiple structurally identical wheel-level control for tire force realization. This modular design offers exceptional configurability, adapting seamlessly to diverse electric vehicle chassis configurations ranging from basic chassis configuration to fully actuated platforms featuring four-wheel independent drive, steering, and braking. To ensure microsecond-level deterministic computation, the vehicle-level controller employs a linearized model within an analytical quadratic programming formulation. At the wheel level, a Piecewise Affine (PWA) tire model with precomputed region-specific Jacobians facilitates efficient real-time linearization. Furthermore, a modified Hildreth’s active-set solver, augmented with Cholesky factorization and physics-informed warm-start strategies, is implemented to exploit spatiotemporal correlations, thereby achieving rapid convergence. High-fidelity CarSim co-simulations of high-speed double lane change maneuvers under varying friction conditions validate the approach. Results demonstrate substantial improvements in yaw rate tracking and sideslip constraint adherence compared to both uncontrolled baselines and conventional integrated control strategies, confirming the effectiveness and scalability of the proposed architecture.

papers.title: On the Performance Boundary of Fourier-Enhanced Physics-Informed Neural Networks for High-Order Nonlinear Oscillators: A MEMS-Motivated Numerical Case Study
papers.abstract: Numerical prediction of high-order nonlinear oscillators using conventional physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) is severely hampered by spectral bias, which prioritizes low-frequency components and leads to significant errors in capturing multi-harmonic vibration responses. This work is a numerical-method-oriented investigation rather than an experimental MEMS validation study. To mitigate spectral-bias issues, we employ a Fourier multiscale physics-informed neural network (FMPINN), which integrates random Fourier feature mapping with a parallel multi-sub-network architecture. We note that the individual building blocks of FMPINN are existing components in scientific-machine-learning literature, and our core contribution is not architectural innovation. While this enhancement yields substantial accuracy improvements—reducing relative L2 errors by one to two orders of magnitude under weak-to-moderate nonlinearity—the central contribution of this work lies in the quantitative characterization of its applicability boundary. Through six systematically designed numerical cases of a fifth-order Duffing oscillator reduced-order model motivated by MEMS resonator dynamics, we demonstrate that the performance of FMPINN saturates under strong nonlinear excitation. Contrary to intuition, simply increasing the Fourier-feature dimension cannot resolve this saturation. Spectral analysis reveals that this bottleneck stems from the initialization-determined finite effective bandwidth of the fixed, frozen frequency mapping, which induces spectral-folding-dominated artifacts in the presence of dense high-order harmonics. This provides a plausible mechanistic interpretation supported by our numerical experiments, rather than a mathematically proven fundamental bound. Our findings establish a practically useful numerical benchmark for the nonlinear stiffness threshold of Fourier-augmented PINN frameworks and underscore the need for adaptive, rather than fixed-scale, frequency embedding strategies. All evaluations are conducted against synthetic noise-free Runge–Kutta 45 benchmarks; experimental MEMS measurement data are not used in the present work.

papers.title: Geometric Modeling and Steady-State Thermal Simulation of TPMS Structures
papers.abstract: Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures provide complex, continuous, and periodic surfaces whose geometric and thermal responses depend on topology and design parameters. This study examines five TPMS families, Gyroid, Diamond, Lidinoid, SplitP, and Schwarz, through implicit geometric modeling and steady-state thermal simulation. The structures were generated in nTop using topology-specific lattice thickness and cell size ranges selected to retain recognizable morphology, surface continuity, and compatibility with the original meshing workflow. Calculated surface area-to-volume ratio (SA/V), maximum temperature (Tmax), and temperature difference (ΔT) were used as geometric and thermal screening metrics. Within the parameter combinations evaluated for each TPMS family, smaller cell sizes and thinner lattice thickness inputs generally increased calculated SA/V. Larger cell sizes or thinner lattice thickness inputs generally increased simulated Tmax and ΔT. The numerical model used homogeneous isotropic Al 6061-T6, a uniform 10 °C base temperature, and a prescribed convection boundary. Simulated temperatures were compared with infrared thermal imaging and surface sensor measurements obtained from 17-4 PH stainless steel specimens under different cooling conditions. Overall, the results demonstrate that topology-specific changes in cell size and lattice thickness input influence both calculated SA/V and steady-state solid conduction response within the evaluated design space. The study provides comparative geometry-to-conduction screening for future investigations of TPMS structures.

papers.title: Reference Data Generation for Remote Sensing Image Classification: A Comprehensive Review of Methods, Challenges, and Recent Advances
papers.abstract: Image classification is a fundamental technique that has been broadly adopted in remote sensing, computer vision and related areas. High-quality annotated datasets are necessary for the development and reliable evaluation of classification and segmentation algorithms for accurate thematic mapping. Reference data are critical in this sense, as their quality has a direct impact on the performance, accuracy and generalization of the model. However, generating reliable reference data remains challenging due to methodological, technical, and annotation-related uncertainties. This study reviews the principal challenges in reference data generation, and the solutions proposed in scientific literature. A total of 100 papers indexed in the Web of Science were examined. The review covers traditional reference data generation methods as well as emerging approaches based on semi-supervised, self-supervised, and active learning, segmentation- and post-processing-assisted labeling, benchmark dataset construction, sampling and accuracy assessment, and deep learning and automated label generation. Major challenges and emerging research directions are also discussed. The results indicate a clear shift from traditional manual techniques to more automated, learning based and accuracy driven methods. The study provides a framework of existing techniques and future research areas in image classification.

papers.title: A Hybrid Gaussian Process-Extreme Gradient Boosting Machine Learning Framework for Robust Knockdown Factor Prediction and Reliability-Based Design of Thin Spherical Shell Caps
papers.abstract: Elastic buckling remains a critical concern in the design of deep spherical shell caps, given that experiments reveal a significant reduction of critical loads from those predicted by linearized eigen-buckling analysis. This discrepancy has been attributed to initial geometric imperfections and is often reconciled through a dimensionless parameter, namely the knockdown factor (KDF). However, conventional KDFs (NASA SP-8007; Eurocode 3) are highly conservative, as they represent the lower bound of an extensive body of experimental data. This study aims to narrow the conservatism in the KDFs for spherical shell caps through machine learning (ML) regression models trained on experimental data on spherical shell buckling. A hybrid model is proposed by combining Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) with Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and its improved performance is demonstrated over conventional ML algorithms, i.e., the Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Support Vector Regressor (SVR), Random Forest Regressor (RFR), and Histogram-based Gradient Boosting (HGBoost). Each of these models uses six input features and a single output, i.e., the KDF. The most critical feature affecting the KDF is ascertained through a sensitivity analysis. The study concludes with a reliability-based design framework that relies on the predictive ML model to obtain safety-consistent, yet less conservative, KDFs.

papers.title: Geometry-Aware Predictive Control for Walk-to-Run Bipedal Obstacle Crossing
papers.abstract: This paper presents a geometry-aware predictive control framework for bipedal obstacle crossing across walking and running regimes. The proposed approach integrates a phase-structured trajectory generator with a constrained model predictive control (MPC) tracking layer to generate coordinated pelvis and swing-foot motions during obstacle traversal. The crossing process is represented through five interpretable phases: pre-crossing, leading-leg clearance, straddle, trailing-leg clearance, and recovery. Within this structure, swing-foot elevation is adapted as a function of obstacle height, while lateral stance widening and pelvis repositioning are introduced as functions of obstacle depth to improve transverse clearance and body alignment. A continuous gait-parameter evolution enables smooth walk-to-run transition without discrete controller switching. The generated references are tracked using MPC to regulate motion smoothness, clearance feasibility, touchdown behavior, and lateral admissibility. The framework is evaluated in reduced-order simulation over five progressively difficult obstacles under walking and running conditions. The robot successfully crosses the first four obstacles, achieving minimum body-obstacle clearances of 0.036, 0.036, 0.059, and 0.017 m, respectively. The fifth and most demanding obstacle leads to collision, identifying the current operating boundary of the proposed reduced-order formulation. Overall, the method provides a compact, interpretable, and computationally efficient basis for intelligent obstacle-aware bipedal locomotion.

papers.title: SIGN-MAPPO: State-Intent-Aware Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Cooperative Driving under Imperfect V2X
papers.abstract: Cooperative driving at mixed-traffic unsignalized intersections is challenged by imperfect vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication, human-driven vehicle (HV) intentions that cannot be directly communicated, and the potential incompatibility of independently generated crossing decisions. This paper proposes State-Intent-Aware Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Cooperative Driving under Imperfect V2X (SIGN-MAPPO) to address these challenges through three coordinated mechanisms. Each decision-eligible connected and automated vehicle (CAV) first reconstructs a receiver-specific traffic graph from its ego state and the peer-state records available to it, from which a shared graph-attention policy generates a raw Stop/Go intention augmented with predicted HV-intent features. CAV intentions are then exchanged through timestamped vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) messages, and a local conflict-aware arbitration layer converts each CAV's intention into a safe executable action despite potentially inconsistent peer information. In the principal Simulation of Urban MObility (SUMO) evaluation, SIGN-MAPPO achieves a 97.53% completion rate, a 0.10% collision rate, and a mean intersection traversal time of 35.28 s. Ablation studies further confirm the complementary contributions of HV-intent prediction and CAV-intent exchange to this performance. The trained policy also remains robust under the evaluated communication-delay and packet-loss ranges, and cross-scenario tests show complete traffic clearance across the tested settings, though safety margins narrow under compound unpredictable HV behavior.

papers.title: PointWalker: Mapless Quadruped Locomotion Directly From Raw LiDAR Point Clouds
papers.abstract: Quadruped robots deployed for inspection and field missions must cross heterogeneous terrain, from stairs, slopes, and gaps to high platforms, stepping stones, and balance beams, where safe support is sparse or see-through. Existing methods interpose a terrain map or a depth image between sensing and control. Maps are costly to maintain, corrupted by odometry drift and outliers, and misled by see-through gratings, while depth cameras degrade with lighting and surface material. In this paper, we present PointWalker, a mapless framework whose single reinforcement learning policy directly consumes raw point clouds from four light detection and ranging (LiDAR) sensors. Voxelized points are encoded by linear self-attention and fused with proprioception through cross-attention, so terrain geometry reaches the policy without maps or foothold estimation. One proximal policy optimization (PPO) run, with terrain-aware rewards and dual-channel simulation of see-through gratings, yields one policy for all seven terrain classes with a 90.1% mean success rate in simulation. Deployed zero-shot on a Deep Robotics X30 at 50 Hz onboard, it crosses 0.8-m gaps, climbs 0.8-m platforms and 45° steel-grating stairs, carries a 50-kg payload, and completes a 2.5-km mountain route.

papers.title: Learning Safety-Constrained Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation for Lunar Surface Operations
papers.abstract: Robotic systems for lunar surface operations must act autonomously and preserve their own integrity in an environment where failures are unrecoverable and continuous supervision is impossible. This paper presents a Constrained Reinforcement Learning framework for quadrupedal mobile manipulators that learns a single whole-body policy for tracking a 6D end-effector pose specified in task space, with operational limits enforced during learning through a constrained learning mechanism. We introduce a reward formulation in which the transition between locomotion and manipulation emerges from the reward geometry rather than from an explicit gating mechanism, a stability term derived from the Gravito-Inertial Inclination Margin and motivated by the reduced-gravity dynamics of the lunar surface, and a design rule for reward regularization that follows from the multiplicative structure of the termination-based objective. The framework is evaluated in a lunar-analog simulation spanning three terrain morphologies at five difficulty levels under lunar gravity, with regolith contact properties calibrated to the JSC-1a simulant and varied from loose to dense. The learned policy attains mean position and orientation errors of 3.22 cm and 6.83 deg. under nominal conditions, retains this precision across regolith densities and over the operationally representative range of terrain difficulty, and reduces soft-constraint violation time by up to an order of magnitude relative to an unconstrained baseline while incurring no hard-constraint violations.

papers.title: Split Conformal Interval Length under Huber Contamination
papers.abstract: Existing analyses of interval length in split conformal prediction largely focus on clean data. However, how contamination at the training and calibration stages alters interval length relative to the corresponding clean population oracle remains understudied. In this paper, we consider Huber contamination and derive a finite-sample upper bound that holds uniformly over contaminating distributions, with leading terms scaling as $L(δ_1+n_1^{-1/2}) +(n_2^{-1/2}+δ_2)/((1-δ_2)r_0)$, in addition to a clean-sample estimation term. We further establish a minimax lower bound matching the upper-bound rate up to constant factors on a regular asymmetric location submodel. For calibration contamination, we obtain an exact worst-case characterization of the population interval-length deviation. We also extend the upper-bound results to conformalized quantile regression and adaptive residual scores. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets provide empirical support for our theoretical findings on training and calibration contamination.

papers.title: World Modeling through Spectral Alignment
papers.abstract: How do we tell a world model what information to preserve? We study this question through the lens of spectral representation learning. We characterize the global optima of the objective, establish conditions for linear recoverability and invariance to nuisance information, and connect temporal-kernel similarity to the behavioral successor measure under an idealized setting. Empirically, the choice of kernel strongly controls which physical quantities are recoverable from the representation. More importantly, temporal spectral alignment improves CEM planning success over LeWorldModel from 52% to 68% on OGBench Cube, 49% to 77% on OGBench Scene, and 29% to 51% on CALVIN. These results suggest that explicitly specifying representation geometry provides a simple way to steer what latent world models preserve for control.

papers.title: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Safety-Aware Haptic Shared Control in Surgical Robotics
papers.abstract: Haptic shared control in surgical robotics combines human-side and robot-side forces at a shared end effector while preserving operator involvement. However, the effects of geometric safety choices on task execution and force coordination remain unclear. We model the interaction as a two-agent cooperative Markov game under centralized training and decentralized execution, comparing learned human control with a task-tuned fixed-impedance baseline. This model-free multi-agent reinforcement learning framework supports joint policy adaptation without requiring a complete analytical interaction model. It compares MADDPG and rMAPPO with an epigraph-constrained approach under common geometric task definitions. In simulation, rMAPPO generally achieved the highest return and tracking performance, whereas the epigraph approach produced more conservative motions and lower geometric exposure, including no observed collision or dangerous-region exposure after geometry transfer. With real operator input, fixed-impedance-trained policies were faster and successful in all recorded trials. Policies trained with a learned partner exhibited greater command opposition, while the fixed epigraph condition produced the most aligned commands. This work provides a benchmark for studying human-control representation and constraint-handling trade-offs in haptic shared control.

papers.title: ANTE: Anticipate, Then Execute -- Learning Internal World Models for Coding Agents from Verified Beliefs
papers.abstract: Rapid advances in large language models have made software engineering agents capable of tackling complex coding tasks. Within a containerized environment, a coding agent receives tool responses or execution results, and determines its later actions by those earlier results. However, most existing coding agents never look ahead: their policies do not anticipate the consequences of actions, and the terminal reward barely attributes a failure to certain earlier steps, so an ill-judged edit can corrupt the repository state irreversibly before any signal arrives. Recent code world models aim to address these challenges, but they are either trained and then frozen before reinforcement learning (RL), or reduced to an auxiliary next-token loss on the environment's outputs. We present ANTE (Anticipate, Then Execute), an agentic RL framework that verifies the policy's pre-action predictions by real execution and turns them into per-step credit for its actions and trust-or-abstain decisions. With an internal belief stated before each action, Belief-Anchored Policy Optimization (BAPO) turns the settled predictions into per-step advantages by anchoring credit on the policy's own forecasts. To turn the trained forecasts into better actions at inference, thereby facilitating effective test-time scaling, ANTE-TTO (test-time optimization) selects among candidate actions without an external scorer. ANTE raises Qwen3-32B from 25.0% to 57.2% pass@1 on SWE-bench Verified, 6.2% above a matched GRPO baseline trained without the belief state; its world model's accuracy climbs from 44% to 69% during RL, and the learned foresight capability transfers across harnesses and out-of-distribution domains. In summary, we aim to build a code world model that knows what has happened, what holds now, and what the next action will achieve.

papers.title: Full Waveform Inversion with a Learned Preconditioner
papers.abstract: Full-waveform inversion (FWI) is a powerful approach for reconstructing subsurface velocity models, but its practical performance is limited by ill-conditioning, sensitivity to the update direction, and the high cost of curvature-based methods. In this project, we investigate whether a neural operator trained on reverse-time-migration (RTM) images can provide a useful learned preconditioner for FWI. We compare projected FWI against neural-preconditioned FWI using either a standard Fourier neural operator (FNO) or a Jacobian-informed FNO (JI-FNO). The neural preconditioner applies the normal operator of the learned RTM map to modify the true Devito FWI gradient. Our experiments show that the JI-FNO preconditioner achieves the lowest model error while maintaining data-residual decay comparable to baseline projected FWI. In contrast, the standard FNO preconditioner is unstable and gives worse model recovery, despite using the same neural-preconditioning framework. We also identify a failure mode of a nonlinear neural Gauss Newton-type inner solve: directly matching the neural RTM output to the FWI gradient creates an objective-space mismatch and does not yield a reliable descent direction. These results suggest that forward RTM-image prediction alone is insufficient for learned preconditioning; accurate learned derivatives and objective-consistent use of the neural operator are critical for producing useful inversion updates.

papers.title: ProWorld: Multi-View World Model with Proprioceptive Feedback for Closed-Loop Policy Evaluation
papers.abstract: Evaluating robot manipulation policies through repeated physical trials is costly. Beyond realistic video, the model must return the camera views and proprioceptive state needed for the policy's next action and preserve failed-action outcomes to avoid overestimating policy capability. We introduce ProWorld, a world model that jointly predicts multi-view video and robot state, then feeds both back to a frozen policy for repeated interaction. ProWorld comprises a shared transformer for joint video-state flow prediction and Shared-Time View Encoding to distinguish cameras while preserving temporal synchronization. To reduce interaction hallucinations that turn missed grasps into successful lifts, we augment training with failed interactions collected in high-fidelity simulation, reducing inflated success rates in the generated environment. ProWorld achieves the highest overall TriWorldBench score among the compared methods. Across three policies and four local manipulation tasks, it attains a Pearson correlation of 0.95 and a Spearman correlation of 0.94 between generated and real success rates. These results support joint visual-proprioceptive feedback and failure-aware training as a basis for world-model-based policy evaluation.

papers.title: LeHami: Symplectic Latent Dynamics for World Models
papers.abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn world models directly in latent space, but unconstrained autoregressive predictors may contract the latent distribution over long rollouts. We introduce Symplectic Hamiltonian JEPA (LeHami), which replaces the standard predictor with an action-conditioned Hamiltonian flow over a structured latent state (q, p) integrated using an exactly symplectic leapfrog step. This construction preserves phase-space volume at every rollout step and rules out uniform contraction, asymptotically stable fixed points, and merging of distinct latent states, independently of the learned parameters or action sequence. We obtain the momentum-like component from temporal derivatives of the learned position-like representation, providing an explicit second-order state for prediction and control. On conservative and actuated visual pendulum environments, LeHami substantially improves long-horizon velocity prediction over an unconstrained JEPA world model and empirically maintains constant latent volume where the baseline contracts. The learned flow also supports accurate integration at unseen sub-frame step sizes and numerical time reversal. These results show how geometric structure can provide inference-time guarantees that are complementary to representation regularization in latent world models.

papers.title: ObsSpec: Accelerating Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Observation Speculation
papers.abstract: Tool-using agents alternate between model generation and tool execution, waiting for each tool call to complete before starting the next generation. This sequential execution is costly during agentic reinforcement learning (RL), which requires large batches of multi-turn rollouts. We introduce ObsSpec, an observation speculation pipeline for agentic RL that uses a small world model to predict tool outputs while the environment executes, allowing the policy to begin its next generation early. ObsSpec retains speculative work only when the predicted and actual observations match exactly, making rollout collection lossless, while co-training keeps the world model up to date as the policy learns. On terminal-use tasks, predictions from a 0.6B world model exactly match actual observations in 66.4% of attempts and arrive roughly 16 times faster. Using these predictions, ObsSpec reduces agent latency by 9.3% and 14.2% for 8B and 32B policies. Across controlled experiments, we characterize the regimes in which ObsSpec reduces agent latency under shared policy resources. Finally, because ObsSpec overlaps policy generation with tool execution, it is architecturally compatible with existing techniques for accelerating RL. Code is available at https://github.com/kylemontgomery1/verl-recipe/tree/obsspec/obsspec.

papers.title: Refinement of the surgical protocol for alveolar ridge augmentation using ring grafts and simultaneous implantation
papers.abstract: Background. Severe horizontal atrophy of the alveolar ridge is a common obstacle to dental implantation. Existing augmentation methods do not always provide predictable results due to insufficient primary stability and high resorption. Refinement of the surgical protocol using ring grafts and simultaneous implantation remains a relevant task. Aim. To describe and clinically substantiate a refined surgical protocol for augmentation of the mandibular alveolar process using ring grafts and simultaneous dental implantation. Materials and methods. The prospective study included 66 patients (25–65 years) with ridge width <4 mm on CBCT. Surgeries were performed using the Meisinger Transfer-Control Plus system for harvesting and fixation of ring grafts (autogenous in 34 patients, allogeneic in 32) with simultaneous placement of Dentium implants. Ridge width was assessed before surgery, immediately after, and at 6 months. Implant stability was measured by resonance frequency analysis (ISQ) at 0, 6, and 12 months. Results. No intraoperative complications occurred. Mean ridge width increased from 3.4±0.1 to 10.4±0.4 mm in the autogenous group and from 2.9±0.4 to 11.1±0.3 mm in the allogeneic group. At 6 months, resorption was 11.5% and 27%, respectively (p<0.05). ISQ values at 12 months reached 80.5±0.1 (autogenous, mandible) and 77.1±0.2 (allogeneic, maxilla), exceeding the clinically acceptable threshold of 65. Conclusion. The proposed protocol provides safe and reproducible ridge width augmentation with high implant stability. Autogenous grafts show less long-term resorption, but allogeneic grafts are also acceptable with careful postoperative management.

papers.title: Selection of surgical protocol for dental implant placement depending on bone density
papers.abstract: Modern dental implantology requires high-precision diagnostic and planning methods to achieve successful implant osseointegration. Key factors determining the long-term stability of the implant are the quality and density of the bone tissue, as well as the choice of optimal surgical technique. Despite significant advances in imaging techniques such as cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), objective assessment of bone density and prediction of implant stability during treatment phases remain challenging. This article presents the results of a clinical study aimed at using radiopaque templates (RT) for accurate assessment of bone density according to Carl E. Misch classification (D1–D4). These templates, created on the basis of a potassium hydrogen phosphate solution with a given concentration and standardized optical density, allow precise determination of bone tissue density and selection of the optimal surgical protocol for implantation. Aim of the study: to substantiate the choice of surgical protocol for dental implant placement to achieve the required primary stability based on the assessment of jaw bone density using potassium hydrogen phosphate solution radiopaque templates. Materials and methods: the study involved 50 patients. All patients underwent preoperative radiological examination using two radiopaque templates with densities corresponding to bone tissue types D1–D2 and D3–D4 on the Carl E. Misch scale. For implantation in D1–D2 type bone tissue, IRIS LM implants (LLC «NPK Likostom», Russia) with a non-aggressive thread (diameter 4 mm, length 10 mm) and a cortical drill at the final stage of bed preparation were used. For implantation in D3–D4 type bone tissue, IRIS Evolution implants (LLC «NPK Likostom», Russia) with aggressive thread (diameter 4 mm, length 10 mm) and bone expanders were used. Primary stability was assessed by ISQ immediately after placement and at 3 months. Results. The combination of additional diagnostic methods in the form of CBCT with RT and ISQ analysis demonstrated the clinical effectiveness of the proposed surgical implant placement protocols depending on bone density.

papers.title: EFEKTIVITAS MEDIA SIMULASI PHET TERHADAP HASIL BELAJAR SISWA KELAS III PADA MATA PELAJARAN MATEMATIKA
papers.abstract: This study aimed to determine the effectiveness of PhET simulation media on the mathematics learning outcomes of third-grade elementary school students on equivalent fractions material. The study employed a quantitative approach using a pre-experimental method with a one-group pretest-posttest design. The participants consisted of 32 third-grade students at SD Negeri Majasem 2, Cirebon City, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through tests, questionnaires, and documentation and analyzed using descriptive statistical techniques and N-Gain analysis. The findings revealed that the use of PhET simulation media positively affected students’ learning outcomes. The average pretest score was 70.31 with a standard deviation of 8.10, while the average posttest score increased to 88.13 with a standard deviation of 6.59. The N-Gain value of 0.60 indicated a moderate level of effectiveness. The improvement occurred because the interactive and visual features of PhET simulations enabled students to explore mathematical concepts more concretely and meaningfully. These findings are supported by the Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning as well as the constructivist theories of Piaget and Vygotsky, which emphasize active learning through visual representation and guided exploration. Therefore, PhET simulation media can serve as an innovative and effective learning tool to improve mathematics achievement among elementary school students.

papers.title: Efektivitas model pembelajaran terhadap kualitas hasil belajar al-qur’an di smp ypkp sentani
papers.abstract: This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of the learning model in improving the quality of Qur'an learning outcomes at YPKP Sentani Junior High School, Jayapura. The approach used is qualitative narrative, with data collection techniques through interviews, observations, and document studies. The results of the study show that the majority of students are not able to read the Qur'an properly and correctly. This condition is influenced by low learning discipline, lack of interest, and the use of less interesting and unvaried learning methods. Learning models such as Problem-Based Learning (PBL) that have been used have not given optimal results, because they are not fully in accordance with the needs of students who still need intensive assistance in mastering the basics of reading the Qur'an. Based on these findings, this study recommends the application of Active Learning and Technology-Enhanced Learning models as alternative approaches that are more appropriate. Strategies such as the use of audiovisual media, video tutorials, and educational games are considered to have the potential to increase student participation, interest, cooperation, and discipline in learning the Qur'an. Adjusting the learning approach to the characteristics of students is considered important to encourage improvement in the quality of learning outcomes in the future
